subject.title: fix(discord): add configurable REST API timeout via channels.discord.apiTimeoutMs

question: Should OpenClaw accept `channels.discord.apiTimeoutMs` as a supported Discord config contract, and if so should maintainers repair this branch or the fuller related timeout PR as the landing base?
rationale: The code change adds a durable public config key, and there are two conflicting branches with different completeness and proof levels, so automation cannot choose the product/API direction safely.

options.title: Repair the fuller timeout branch
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93222 as the preferred landing base once conflicts and normal merge gates are resolved.

options.title: Bring this branch to parity
options.body: Keep this PR as the base only if it is updated with monitor wiring, generated metadata, docs/UI hints, focused tests, and real behavior proof.

options.title: Defer the public knob
options.body: Close or pause both branches if maintainers prefer internal default/retry tuning instead of adding a new long-term config surface.

recommendation.title: Repair the fuller timeout branch
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93222 as the preferred landing base once conflicts and normal merge gates are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is recent ownership of the Discord REST/client implementation and timeout behavior.
